content: Neuro Mates is an AI- and IoT-enabled smart-care project focused on Parkinson’s, Alzheimer’s, Epilepsy, and physiotherapy support for paralysis-related movement limitations and Parkinson’s. It combines sensor-based monitoring, software workflows, alerts, reminders, activity records, and interactive rehabilitation support.

Neuro Mates aims to build a connected, accessible, patient-centred care-support ecosystem that helps patients, families, caregivers, and healthcare professionals stay informed and connected. Its mission is to use practical AI, IoT, embedded systems, and software to support everyday monitoring, communication, reminders, record keeping, and rehabilitation workflows. It does not replace doctors or professional treatment.

Neurological conditions and mobility limitations can create ongoing care needs beyond clinic visits. Patients and families may need support with routine monitoring, unusual-event awareness, location safety, reminders, activity records, and communication. Neuro Mates is designed to support selected parts of these everyday workflows.

The platform is designed around four roles: Patient, Caretaker, Doctor, and Admin. Patient features may include relevant personal monitoring, reminders, activities, and rehabilitation interactions. Caretakers may receive relevant alerts and updates. Doctors may review relevant records and reports. Admin is a platform-level role; detailed functions are not specified. Do not invent permissions or features.

A typical workflow is: a wearable or sensor collects a signal; a controller forwards data to software; software processes, visualizes, or records it; relevant alerts or reminders are presented to the patient or authorized caregiver; and authorized users review available records. Exact steps differ by module.

Discussed technologies include Python, Django, FastAPI, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, SQLite, ESP32, Arduino UNO R4 Minima, MPU6050, NEO-6M GPS, BioAmp EXG Pill, Muscle BioAmp Shield, WhatsApp notifications, AI/ML, and signal processing. This list does not prove every component is integrated or production deployed.

The Parkinson’s module is designed for movement-related monitoring and care support. Its wearable concept uses ESP32 and MPU6050 and is worn on the dorsal side (back side) of the hand. Software concepts include movement/orientation visualization, unusual-movement indicators, fall-event history, alerts, and rehabilitation activity support.

The Parkinson’s wearable concept uses an ESP32 controller and MPU6050 accelerometer/gyroscope. It is worn on the dorsal side (back) of the hand with an adjustable strap. Fingers, thumb, palm, and wrist remain free. Do not describe it as a smartwatch, palm device, or forearm band.

The Parkinson’s software concept includes motion and orientation visualization, review of tremor or unusual-movement indicators, fall-event history, timestamps, and rehabilitation activity records. Discussed software direction: Django backend, SQLite, and HTML/CSS/JavaScript frontend. No verified accuracy figure is available.

The Parkinson’s alert flow is movement monitoring, sensor-data analysis, a potentially concerning event, WhatsApp notification and/or siren, then continued monitoring and status confirmation where implemented. An alert is not a diagnosis and does not guarantee fall or tremor detection.

The Alzheimer’s module is designed to support location awareness, activity logging, memory-recall prompts, and routine reminders. Its wearable concept uses ESP32 and NEO-6M GPS and is worn on the outer upper arm, slightly below the shoulder.

The Alzheimer’s wearable concept uses ESP32 and NEO-6M GPS. Intended placement is the outer side of the upper arm, slightly below the shoulder, using an adjustable breathable band. Do not place it on the top of the shoulder, neck, wrist, waist, or chest.

The Alzheimer’s concept includes GPS location monitoring and a discussed 1 km safe-zone boundary. If a patient moves outside the configured boundary, the system is intended to notify the caregiver. GPS accuracy, refresh rate, and alert latency depend on implementation and testing; do not promise perfect continuous tracking.

The Alzheimer’s software concept includes activity logging every two hours from 8 AM to 10 PM, next-day memory-recall questions based on activity, family-photo prompts, medication/activity reminders, missed-activity alerts, and reports. These are not proven memory therapy or treatment.

The Alzheimer’s software concept includes a location view and safe-zone boundary, daily activity timeline, memory quiz, family-photo prompts, medication/activity reminders, missed-activity notifications, and reports. Discussed software direction: FastAPI, SQLite, HTML/CSS/JavaScript. Workflow: Track → Record → Remember → Remind → Share.

The Epilepsy module is designed around EEG-related signal monitoring, potentially abnormal activity awareness, caregiver notification, and event records. Hardware concept: ESP32 and BioAmp EXG Pill. Wearable concept: lightweight adjustable headband with the specified electrode reference point behind the ear, contacting skin.

The Epilepsy wearable concept combines ESP32 and BioAmp EXG Pill for EEG-related electrical signal acquisition. It uses a lightweight adjustable headband. The specified electrode reference point is behind the ear and should contact skin. Do not obstruct eyes or hearing or invent additional electrode positions.

The Epilepsy software concept includes EEG waveform visualization, signal history and timestamps, review of potentially abnormal activity, caregiver alerts, siren status, continued monitoring, and normal-state confirmation where implemented. It also includes a seizure diary and medication/appointment reminders. Discussed software direction: FastAPI, SQLite, HTML/CSS/JavaScript.

Epilepsy workflow: Monitor → Detect → Alert → Recover → Resume. The concept monitors EEG-related signals, identifies activity that may need attention, sends a WhatsApp caretaker alert and activates a siren where configured, continues monitoring, and records recovery or normal-state status where available. It does not confirm or prevent seizures.

The physiotherapy module supports interactive rehabilitation exercises for face, hand/fingers, and legs for paralysis-related movement limitations and Parkinson’s. It combines biomedical electrical-signal sensing with game-based exercise interactions and activity records. It does not replace a physiotherapist.

The physiotherapy concept uses Arduino UNO R4 Minima and/or ESP32, BioAmp EXG Pill, and Muscle BioAmp Shield. Biomedical electrodes are attached to appropriate muscle areas for the selected exercise, with wires connected to sensing modules and controller. Electrode placement must follow the actual hardware configuration and qualified guidance.

The physiotherapy games include face actions such as smiling or raising eyebrows; hand/finger actions such as opening and closing the hand, finger movement, or gripping; and selected leg movements. Exercise selection, difficulty, repetitions, and progression should follow professional guidance.

The physiotherapy software concept presents interactive exercise games, relevant signal or muscle-activity visualization, session progress, and activity records for face, hand, and leg exercise areas. A game score is not proof of clinical recovery and the system does not cure paralysis.

The Patient portal is intended to show personal monitoring views, reminders, activities, and rehabilitation interactions relevant to the assigned care module. Exact features depend on the module and implemented permissions.

The Caretaker portal is intended for authorized family members or caregivers to receive relevant notifications and follow available patient updates, such as location alerts, movement or EEG-related alerts, reminders, and activity records depending on the module.

The Doctor portal is intended to make relevant monitoring records, activity histories, and reports available for professional review. It does not automatically make clinical decisions, replace examination, or provide diagnosis.
The Admin portal is a platform-level role. Specific admin capabilities have not been fully specified. Do not invent billing, staff management, hospital management, or clinical approval functions.

Patient-related data may include location, activity records, wearable signals, reminders, and caregiver notifications. A production deployment should implement authentication, role-based authorization, secure transmission and storage, consent, data minimization, and retention policies. These are recommended requirements unless verified as implemented.

Neuro Mates is a care-support and monitoring project, not a diagnostic or treatment replacement. Do not provide definitive diagnosis, promise prevention, guarantee seizure/fall detection, recommend medication changes, or tell users to ignore urgent symptoms. Direct medical questions to qualified professionals and urgent situations to local emergency services.

Available project information describes concepts, hardware choices, software directions, and intended workflows. It does not provide verified deployment status, clinical validation, regulatory approval, measured accuracy, production uptime, or quantified impact. Use cautious wording unless the team supplies evidence.

Q: What is Neuro Mates? A: An AI- and IoT-enabled smart-care project designed to support Parkinson’s, Alzheimer’s, Epilepsy, and paralysis-focused rehabilitation through monitoring, alerts, reminders, records, and interactive exercise support.

Q: Which conditions does Neuro Mates focus on? A: Parkinson’s, Alzheimer’s, Epilepsy, and physiotherapy support for paralysis-related movement limitations and Parkinson’s. This does not mean the system treats or cures these conditions.
Q: Who can use the platform? A: The platform is designed around Patient, Caretaker, Doctor, and Admin roles. Available features depend on authorization and implementation.
Q: What devices are discussed? A: ESP32, Arduino UNO R4 Minima, MPU6050, NEO-6M GPS, BioAmp EXG Pill, and Muscle BioAmp Shield. Each module uses relevant components only.
Q: Where is the Parkinson’s wearable worn? A: On the dorsal side, or back side, of the hand. It uses an ESP32 and MPU6050 in the discussed concept.
Q: Where is the Alzheimer’s wearable worn? A: On the outer upper arm, slightly below the shoulder. It uses an ESP32 and NEO-6M GPS in the discussed concept.
Q: Where is the Epilepsy electrode reference point? A: Behind the ear, contacting the skin, according to the specified headband concept. The system does not confirm a seizure.
Q: What exercises are included? A: Interactive face, hand/finger, and leg exercise games supported by biomedical signal sensing in the discussed concept.
Q: Can Neuro Mates diagnose a neurological condition? A: No. It is a monitoring and care-support project, not a diagnostic device.
Q: Does an alert confirm a medical emergency? A: No. It indicates an event that may need attention under configured rules. Follow professional advice and local emergency guidance.
Q: What is the accuracy of Neuro Mates? A: No verified accuracy figure has been supplied. The chatbot must not invent a percentage.
Q: Can Neuro Mates replace a doctor or physiotherapist? A: No. Diagnosis, treatment decisions, and rehabilitation planning remain with qualified professionals.
Q: How can I contact the team? A: Use the website’s verified Contact Us or Register for a Demo section. No verified public contact details were supplied for this dataset.

The long-term direction is to develop the four care areas into a coordinated platform, improve sensor-data and software workflows, strengthen patient-caregiver-doctor communication, and refine interactive rehabilitation support. Do not invent roadmap dates, partnerships, regulatory milestones, or commercial promises.

The chatbot must answer project questions from retrieved Neuro Mates content, say when details are unavailable, distinguish planned concepts from verified features, avoid unsupported medical and performance claims, protect private patient data, and direct urgent medical concerns to local emergency services or qualified professionals.
